steps.text:
Materials Needed: New Unit Tiles: ANG, ING, ONG, UNG, ANK, INK, ONK, UNK. Letter Tiles: A-Z plus CH, TH, CK, SH, WH. Extra F, S, L, Z.

Overview: Students learn two new sets of Units (ending in NG and NK). Units are 3 letters that appear at the end of a word and make a slightly different sound as a group than individually. It is critical to emphasize there is NO 'ENG' or 'ENK' tile. The /eeng/ sound is spelled ING. Mark units by drawing a box around them.
Repeat this nonsense word, then make just its FIRST sound. Ready? FRACK.
Expected: Frack, /f/
Point to the tile that makes that sound.
Student points to the F tile.
Now I want the LAST sound. KEZZ.
Expected: Kez, /z/
Point to that tile.
Student points to Z.
Now for the MIDDLE sound. Say both the sound AND its keyword. Ready? COSK.
Expected: Cosk, /o/-Olive.
Repeat First Sound for: RUCK, THISK, WHOSK. Last Sound for: CLITH, BLASH, QUECH, BLEV. Vowel Sound for: SPILK, BUSK, SHELK, GLACK.

sections.title: D: NEW TEACHING #1: The NG Units

steps.text: What does this say?
Expected: ALL
Is it a Digraph or a Unit?
Expected: Unit. Because it's red and makes an unusual sound.
Where do Units come in a word—at the beginning or at the end?
Expected: At the end.
Right. Today, you're going to learn several more Units.
You probably already know these. What do they say?
Expected: /ang/, /ing/, /ong/, /ung/.
Let's make words with these Units.
What does this say? And if you were finger spelling it, how many fingers would you use?
Expected: Sing. Two fingers. One for /s/, one for /ing/.
Let's create words that start with a Digraph.
Student reads THING. Change ING to ONG to read THONG.
Saying these units is easy. But spelling them can be tricky. Look at the Unit tiles. Is there one that starts with an E?
Expected: No.
There is NO E-N-G. So when you hear /eeng/, how are you going to spell it?
Expected: I-N-G.

sections.title: E: NEW TEACHING #2: The NK Units

steps.text: Now I'm going to show you 4 more Units.
What's the same about ANG and ANK? What's different?
Expected: Both start with A-N. One ends in G, the other in K.
Why did they spell /k/ with a K and not a C-K?
Expected: Because you only use CK right after a Short Vowel! This is a Unit, so the vowel isn't making its normal short sound.
Exactly. Be sure to make the /k/ sound loudly when you're saying the ones in this column. Let's make words.
Student reads SANK. Tutor swaps to SINK, SONK, SUNK.
Let's try a 3-letter blend.
What does that say? And is it a Closed Syllable?
Expected: Shrink. No, it's a Unit Syllable because it contains a Unit and the vowel isn't making its normal short sound.
By the way, is there an E-N-K?
Expected: No. You spell /eenk/ with I-N-K.

sections.title: F: Spell Real Words with Fingers, then Tiles

steps.text: Now you're going to finger spell. The first word is FRANK. Repeat that word.
Expected: FRANK
Use your fingers to break it into sounds. But raise only ONE finger for the ANK sound, because you bring down only one tile.
Student raises thumb for /f/, index for /r/, middle for /ank/.
Double check by blending those sounds. Now change one tile to make it say PRANK.
Student swaps F for P.
Dictate the remaining words, changing one tile at a time: LUNG, LONG, SLUNK, STUNG, DRANK, DRINK, CLUNG, SLUNG.

sections.title: I: Read Words Through Word Frame

steps.text: Now you're going to read words through the word frame. If you know the word for sure, just say it. Otherwise, sound it out.

sections.title: J: Spell Words with Fingers, then Paper

steps.text: After you finger spell these words, you'll write them on paper. The first word is WING.
Expected: WING
Use your fingers. Raise only ONE finger for the ING sound. Now say-and-write each sound on paper.
Student writes W, ING.
Dictate Real Words: KING, BANG, RANK, BLINK, DUNK. Dictate Nonsense Words: RONK, SPRINK, FLANG, GRONG, SMUNK.

sections.title: K: Read NEW Sight Word List

steps.text: Let's look at some more common Sight words to see which ones we need to practice.
For any words the student misses, create a new index card. Have the student draw a visual clue in the lower-left corner to help them remember.
Let's read some phrases. Tell me the WHO, DID WHAT, WHERE, and ADD-ON phrases.
Now find every word that ends in a Unit, and box off the Unit on the screen.

sections.title: N: Spell Phrases and Sight Words on Paper

steps.text: Now you're going to write some phrases. The first phrase is THE STRONG KING. Repeat that phrase.
Expected: THE STRONG KING
Write it down. Double check by reading exactly what you wrote.
Dictate remaining phrases: A LONG STRING, BRING THAT THING. Then dictate the 3 tricky sight words you made cards for earlier.
Now you'll read some sentences. Read the first sentence to yourself, then read it out loud.

payload: Frank flung the ring from his hand in to the sink.
Kent swung the bat in the thick fog and hit the ball.
When the ship sank, Dick and Chet clung to the rock in the big pond.
Jack slept in the long bunk next to the strong king.
Hank sang a song as he hung up his smock which stunk.
If Scott does flunk this test, he will not pass the class.
I think the mink dress will shrink.
They drank the strong drink with a chunk of crisp crust.

steps.text: Mark the WHO phrase, DID WHAT phrase, WHERE phrase, and ADD-ON phrase.
Student marks phrases and reads sentence with phrasing (pausing between chunks).
Now you're going to write three sentences. The first sentence is: THE STRONG KING KEPT TRACK OF HIS TRUNK.
Expected: THE STRONG KING KEPT TRACK OF HIS TRUNK.
Check your sentence. Does it start with a capital and end with punctuation?

Dictate: FRANK DRANK THE MILK WITH HIS LUNCH. 
Dictate: HANK WILL BRING A SNACK TO MATH CLASS.
Now you're ready to read a story. Preread the story and figure out the tough words. Then read it out loud to me.

payload.title: The Finch
payload.text: If I were a finch I think I would have fun. In the spring, I would sit on a branch and bask in the sun. I could get some string and a twig or a stick and fix a nest. I would sing a long song. Some one would get a lift from the song. They would clap and fling a kiss. Next, I would nod, tuck in a wing, and get a rest.

steps.text: Have the student retell the story in their own words to check comprehension.
